items.english: ‘You won’t listen, will you.’ The young father gazed at the small round arms and at the child’s eyes with long, darkish lashes, moving nimbly, cleverly, without a pause, as if wondering what was to be done, then with a smile over his whole face, pinching the child’s round, stuck-out cheek lightly with his finger, he took a big bowl from under the {t:table} as if feeling for it and put it in the child’s hand.
notes: 彼女の手 is the child's hand receiving the bowl (p7 child, not mother), so rendered as the child's hand per bible rather than ambiguous her to avoid resolving mother/child pronoun by pronoun alone.
怜悧《れいり》read as cleverly and 微笑《ほゝゑみ》 as smile to keep smile network; face-full smile kept literal against ennoblement.

sentences: 若い父親は、その小さなまるい腕や、敏捷に怜悧にすきもなく動いてる、黒みがちの睫のながい子供の瞳をぢっと見てゐると、どうしたらいゝだらうといふやうに、やがて顔一ぱいな微笑を持って、子供のまるくつき出た頬を指で一寸つまみながら、大きな茶碗をテーブルの下から探すやうにしてとると、彼女の手に渡した。

items.english: She served the hot, freshly cooked {t:rice}, with white steam rising thick from it, from the pot and handed it to him. And her young large eyes too, full of a mother’s joy, gazed at the child, never still for a moment, lovely as a small bird. And as if she could not bear it, muttering to herself, whatever is the matter with this child, as if the child were dear beyond help, she said firmly, ‘{t:boya},’ but the smile overflowed her face, and she looked at the man’s face as if asking for help. And the three, as if they had forgotten everything, smiled at each other as if wondering what to do for the child. And for the child’s sake they began the meal with a warm bustle, and with a smile and joy overflowing of itself on top of it. And for the clattering noise they did not hear the sound of rain and wind.
notes: 口の中に独言 kept as muttering to herself to hold inner speech distinct from quoted ‘{t:boya},’ without adding explained emotion.
雨風の音 kept literally as sound of rain and wind, not storm, to preserve middle forgetting of storm (p8) against frame p1/p19/p38; verbally linked but not underlined.
笑/笑み/笑ひ kept as smile throughout to hold thread to table laughter and later vision smile; not varied to laugh/grin.

sentences: 彼女は鍋から熱い炊き立ての、白い湯気が一ぱい立ち上ってる御飯をついで彼に渡した。
そして彼女の若い大きな瞳も、母親らしい嬉しさにみちて子供の瞬間もぢっとしてない、小鳥のやうに愛らしい様子を見つめた。
そして、たまらなささうに、この子はどうしたといふんだらう、とふと口の中に独言を云ひながら、どうにも仕方がない程可愛いといふやうな様子で、『坊や、』と強く云ったけれども、笑が顔からあふれて了って、彼女は助をかりるやうに男の顔を見た。
そして三人は、すべての事を忘れてしまった様に、子供の為めに互にどうしようかといふ様に笑ひ合った。
そして子供の為めに、彼等は暖かい賑かさと、其上に自然に溢れる笑ひと嬉しさを持って食事にとりかゝったのであった。
また彼等は、ごたごたした騒がしさの為に、雨風の音を耳にしない。

items.english: The young father spread his red, big hand busily over the {t:table}. And holding back the smile the child made well up in spite of himself, he held the child up and put a little food into that small red mouth. In the gaps, he hurriedly opened his big mouth, he crammed {t:rice} into his own mouth.
notes: Repeated彼は kept as repeated he in final sentence to keep additive, slightly awkward syntax rather than rationalising into one clause.
笑 kept as smile held back, linking to p7-p8 parental smiles; big red hand and big mouth kept literal as physical counterweight, not softened.

sentences: 若い父親は、彼の赤く大きな片手を忙しくテーブルの上に拡げてゐた。
そしてその眼は子供によって仕方がなく湧き出た笑を堪へながら、子供をさゝへて、その小さな赤い口に僅の食物を入れてやった。
そのすきに彼は、あわたゞしく大きな口を開けた、彼は彼自身の口のなかに御飯を押し込んだ。

data.say: Drafted p7-p9 in spare close voice keeping smile/table/rice/boya tokens and literal bustle against vision to come.
